title: Mkode Store
desc: A complete, production-ready digital storefront built with React and Django REST Framework, featuring secure JWT authentication and Razorpay payment integration.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Mkode Store is a comprehensive digital asset marketplace. It serves as an end-to-end e-commerce solution, allowing users to browse projects, add items to a secure cart, and complete purchases using the Razorpay payment gateway.

sections.title: The Problem
sections.content: Building a secure digital storefront requires balancing complex payment processing, reliable user authentication, and fast media delivery. Monolithic architectures often struggle to scale these distinct concerns efficiently without becoming rigid and difficult to maintain.

subsections.title: Decoupled Architecture
subsections.content: Utilized Django REST Framework to build a robust, scalable backend API completely decoupled from the responsive React frontend, allowing independent scaling and complex client-side state management for shopping carts.

subsections.title: Auth & Payments
subsections.content: Implemented stateless JWT authentication for secure session management alongside a rigorous Razorpay checkout flow that relies on strict cryptographic signature verification on the backend to prevent tampering.

subsections.title: Media Optimization
subsections.content: Developed an automated, on-the-fly Python image compression pipeline using Pillow that converts user uploads to WebP format, significantly reducing payload bandwidth and improving frontend rendering times.

sections.title: Key Features
content_items: Secure user registration and JWT authentication
Integrated Razorpay checkout flow with signature verification
Admin dashboard for revenue and customer analytics
Automated on-the-fly image compression to WebP

title: Tic Tac Toe Game
tagline: Graphical game with custom UI engine and AI opponent
desc: A complete graphical implementation of Tic Tac Toe built with Python's Turtle module, featuring a custom-built UI engine, persistent statistics, and a heuristic AI opponent.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Tic Tac Toe Game is a comprehensive graphical game built entirely from scratch using Python's Turtle graphics library. It bypasses standard GUI frameworks by implementing its own custom rendering engine to handle interactive buttons, modal dialogs, and smooth animations, while maintaining lifetime player statistics via local file storage.

subsections.title: Custom UI Engine
subsections.content: Developed a custom graphics pipeline with manual tracer control to draw rounded rectangles with drop shadows. The engine includes an event listener system that registers button coordinates and maps physical mouse clicks to logical UI actions.

subsections.title: Heuristic AI Engine
subsections.content: Built a priority-based AI opponent for single-player mode. The algorithm evaluates the board state on every turn, prioritizing instant wins, then blocking immediate player threats, before falling back to center-control or random availability.

subsections.title: Data Persistence
subsections.content: Engineered a local storage layer using Python's native JSON module. The game seamlessly loads and saves lifetime statistics (wins, losses, draws) for both PvP and PvAI game modes, displaying them on a dedicated leaderboard screen.

content_items.title: Coordinate Mapping
content_items.desc: Translated complex, pixel-perfect screen coordinates (e.g., x: -200, y: 150) from the user's mouse clicks into a normalized 0-8 logical grid index to accurately update the underlying game state array.

content_items.title: Animation Handling
content_items.desc: Implemented frame-by-frame iterative drawing for the winning line animation. Using a dedicated 'anim_pen' and controlled time-sleeps prevented the main application loop from freezing during state transitions.

sections.title: Key Features
content_items: Single Player (AI) and Two Player (PvP) modes
Decoupled rendering controllers (UI, Game, Animation, Popup)
Dynamic modal overlays for game-over states

title: Watermark Studio
tagline: Desktop & Web Hybrid — Professional Branding Utility
desc: A dual-platform branding tool (Desktop EXE + Streamlit Cloud) designed for high-performance batch image processing with professional alpha-compositing.

sections.title: Solution Overview
sections.content: Watermark Studio is a professional-grade utility designed to solve the problem of manual image branding. It evolved from a Tkinter desktop automation tool into a hybrid suite, offering a native Windows installer (Inno Setup) and a global cloud-hosted web application.

subsections.title: Pixel-Perfect Alpha Compositing
subsections.content: The core engine utilizes the Pillow (PIL) library to perform complex alpha-blending. It handles various watermark modes (text/logo) and uses coordinate-mapping to ensure the watermark remains proportionate across different image resolutions.

subsections.title: Cross-Platform Strategy
subsections.content: The project demonstrates versatility in deployment: the desktop version provides high-speed local processing for hundreds of images, while the Streamlit web version offers an instant, zero-installation branding experience for quick edits.

sections.title: Key Achievements
content_items: Optimized batch loop processing with low memory footprint
Implemented High-DPI support for Windows 10/11 environments
Developed a custom 'Smart Slider' component for intuitive opacity control
Successful Cloud deployment with automated requirements management

title: Snake Game
desc: A study in game loop architecture and collision detection algorithms.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: A faithful recreation of the classic arcade Snake game. This project explores the fundamentals of game development, including the main game loop and collision detection algorithms, and real-time user input handling.

content_items.title: Input Latency (The Suicide Bug)
content_items.desc: If a player pressed 'Down' then 'Left' faster than one game tick, the snake would turn into itself and die immediately. I solved this by buffering input commands.
